content: 1. A randomized controlled trial was conducted to investigate the reversal of mild balance dysfunction in older adults. The study was published in Physical Therapy in 2012, volume 92, issue 1, pages 24–37. 2. Wolf SL, O'Grady M, Easley KA, Guo Y, Kressig RW, and Kutner M examined the effects of intense Tai Chi training on physical performance and hemodynamic outcomes in older adults who were considered transitionally frail. This study was published in the Journal of Gerontology: Biological Sciences and Medical Sciences in 2006, volume 61, issue 2, pages 184–189. 3. Logghe IHJ, Zeeuwe PEM, Verhagen AP, Wijnen-Sponselee RMT, Willemsen SP, Bierma-Zeinstra SMA, van Rossum E, Faber MJ, and Koes BW conducted a randomized clinical trial to assess the effectiveness of Tai Chi Chuan in preventing falls among elderly individuals living at home. The findings were published in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Society in 2009, volume 57, issue 1, pages 70–75. 4. Wolf SL, Sattin RW, Kutner M, O'Grady M, Greenspan AI, and Gregor RJ evaluated the impact of intense Tai Chi exercise training on fall occurrences in older, transitionally frail adults. This randomized controlled trial was published in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Society in 2003, volume 51, issue 12, pages 1693–1701. 5. Baker MK, Atlantis E, and Singh MAF reviewed multi-modal exercise programs for older adults. Their findings were published in Age and Ageing in 2007, volume 36, issue 4, pages 375–381. 6. Blankevoort CG, van Heuvelen MJ, Boersma F, Luning H, de Jong J, and Scherder EJ reviewed the effects of physical activity on strength, balance, mobility, and activities of daily living (ADL) performance in elderly individuals with dementia. This review was published in Dementia and Geriatric Cognitive Disorders in 2010, volume 30, issue 5, pages 392–402. 7. Chan WC, Yeung JWF, Wong CSM, et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy of physical exercise in preventing falls among older adults with cognitive impairment. The study was published in the Journal of the American Medical Directors Association in 2015, volume 16, issue 2, pages 149–154. 8. Chin APMJ, Van Uffelen JGZ, Riphagen I, et al. systematically reviewed the functional effects of physical exercise training in frail older adults. Their findings were published in Sports Medicine in 2008, volume 38, issue 9, pages 781–793. 9. Chudyk AM, Jutai JW, Petrella RJ, and Speechley M conducted a systematic review of hip fracture rehabilitation practices in the elderly. This review was published in Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 2009, volume 90, issue 2, pages 246–262. 10. Coelho FGdM, Santos-Galduroz RF, Gobbi S, and Stella F reviewed the effects of systematized physical activity on cognitive performance in elderly individuals with Alzheimer's dementia. The study was published in the Revista Brasileira de Psiquiatria in 2009, volume 31, issue 2, pages 163–170. 11. Costello E and Edelstein JE provided an update on falls prevention for community-dwelling older adults, reviewing single and multifactorial intervention programs. This review was published in the Journal of Rehabilitation Research and Development in 2008, volume 45, issue 8, pages 1135–1152. 12. Davis JC, Robertson MC, Ashe MC, Liu-Ambrose T, and Khan KM systematically reviewed the economic evaluations of falls prevention interventions for individuals aged 80 years and older. Their findings were published in the British Journal of Sports Medicine in 2010, volume 44, issue 2, pages 80–89. 13. Forster A, Lambley R, and Young JB reviewed the effectiveness of physical rehabilitation for older adults in long-term care. This systematic review was published in Age and Ageing in 2010, volume 39, issue 2, pages 169–175. 14. Goodwin VA, Abbott RA, Whear R, Bethel A, Ukoumunne OC, Thompson-Coon J, and Stein K conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of multiple-component interventions for preventing falls and fall-related injuries among older adults. This study was published in BMC Geriatrics in 2014, volume 14, article 15. 15. Harmer P and Li F reviewed the role of Tai Chi in falls prevention among older adults. Their findings were published in Medicine and Sport Science in 2008, volume 52, pages 124–134. 16. Heyn PC, Johnson KE, and Kramer AF conducted a meta-analysis on the outcomes of endurance and strength training in cognitively impaired and cognitively intact older adults. This study was published in the Journal of Nutrition, Health, and Aging in 2008, volume 12, issue 6, pages 401–409. 17. Heyn P, Abreu BC, and Ottenbacher KJ reviewed the effects of exercise training on elderly individuals with cognitive impairment and dementia. This meta-analysis was published in Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 2004, volume 85, issue 10, pages 1694–1704. 18. Keyser JJ critically reviewed the scientific evidence on whether late-life physical activity or exercise prevents or minimizes disability. This review was published in the American Journal of Preventive Medicine in 2003, volume 25, issue 3 Supplement 2, pages 129–136. 19. Lee MS, Pittler MH, Shin BC, and Ernst E systematically reviewed the effects of Tai Chi on osteoporosis. This study was published in Osteoporosis International in 2008, volume 19, issue 2, pages 139–146. 20. Liu C and Latham N reviewed the effects of progressive resistance strength training on improving physical function in older adults. This Cochrane systematic review was published in 2009, issue 3, article CD002759. 21. Liu C-J, Shiroy DM, Jones LY, and Clark DO systematically reviewed the effects of functional training on muscle strength, physical functioning, and activities of daily living in older adults. This review was published in the European Review of Aging and Physical Activity in 2014, volume 11, pages 95–106. 22. Liu-Ambrose T and Donaldson MG reviewed the role of resistance training programs in improving cognition among older adults. This narrative review was published in the British Journal of Sports Medicine in 2009, volume 43, issue 1, pages 25–27. 23. Littbrand H, Stenvall M, and Rosendahl E systematically reviewed the applicability and effects of physical exercise on physical and cognitive functions and activities of daily living among individuals with dementia. This study was published in the American Journal of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 2011, volume 90, issue 6, pages 495–518.
